title: Amazon Textract now available in Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich)
body:
Amazon Textract is now available in the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Zurich) Regions. Amazon Textract is a machine learning service that automatically extracts text, handwriting, and data from scanned documents, going beyond simple optical character recognition (OCR) to identify and extract text and structured data. 
 At launch in these Regions, Amazon Textract supports text detection and document analysis. This includes the DetectDocumentText, AnalyzeDocument, StartDocumentTextDetection, GetDocumentTextDetection, StartDocumentAnalysis, and GetDocumentAnalysis operations. The AnalyzeExpense, AnalyzeID, and AnalyzeLending operations, and Custom Queries (adapters), are not available in these Regions at this time. 
 With this launch, Amazon Textract is available in a total of 18 AWS Regions: US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), Europe (Spain), the AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West) Regions, and the newly added Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe

title: Announcing AWS for Fluent Bit 3.0.0 based on Fluent Bit 4.1.1
body: AWS for Fluent Bit announces version  3.0.0 , based on Fluent Bit version 4.1.1 and Amazon Linux 2023. Container logging using AWS for Fluent Bit is now more performant and more feature-rich for AWS customers, including those using  Amazon Elastic Container Services  (Amazon ECS) and  Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service  (Amazon EKS).    AWS for Fluent Bit enables Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS customers to collect, process, and route container logs to destinations including Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, and Amazon S3 without changing application code. AWS for Fluent Bit 3.0.0 upgrades the Fluent Bit version to 4.1.1, and upgrades the base image to Amazon Linux 2023. These updates deliver access to the latest Fluent Bit features, significant performance improvements, and enhanced security. New features include native OpenTelemetry (OTel) support for ingesting and forwarding OTLP logs, metrics, and traces with AWS SigV4 authentication. Performance improvements include faster JSON parsing, processing more logs per vCPU with lower latency. Security enhancements include TLS min version and cipher controls, which enforce your TLS policy on outputs f

title: Announcing an updated text detection model for Amazon Textract
body:
Amazon Textract now provides an updated text detection model that improves accuracy, expands language support, and enhances multilingual table extraction. The updated model applies to the DetectDocumentText and AnalyzeDocument APIs and requires no changes to your Amazon Textract API requests or response schema. Your applications are served by the updated model automatically, so you can continue calling Amazon Textract exactly as before. 
 The updated model expands language coverage to more than 40 languages, including Albanian, Arabic, Basque, Belarusian, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latvian, Lithuanian, Luxembourgish, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Serbian Cyrillic, Serbian Latin, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Turkmen, and Ukrainian, enabling reliable processing of previously unsupported scripts. Accuracy improvements include enhanced long-word recognition and handwriting detection. Additionally, multilingual table extraction is more robust on merged cells, skewed or rotated table

title: Amazon CloudFront now supports self-service increases in AWS Service Quotas
body:
Amazon CloudFront now supports AWS Service Quotas, so you can view, monitor, and request increases for 28 CloudFront quotas from the Service Quotas console or API.  
 Until now, increasing a quota on resources such as distributions, cache policies, origins, or alternate domain names meant opening a support case and waiting for manual review. If you have AWS Business Support or higher, requests for limit increases within published thresholds are now approved automatically. For example, you can raise your distribution quota from 500 to 1,000, or the number of alternate domain names per distribution from 100 to 500, without opening a support case. Some quotas also publish usage metrics to Amazon CloudWatch every 5 minutes, so you can set alarms and request an increase before you reach a limit..  
 This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon CloudFront is supported.  
 To get started, visit  the Service Quotas console  to view and request increases for your CloudFront quotas. To learn more, see  Amazon CloudFront quotas  in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide.

title: Amazon Bedrock expands API support and introduces Cross-Region Inferencing for OpenAI models in AWS GovCloud (US)
body:
Amazon Bedrock now supports the OpenAI GPT-5.6 models (Terra and Luna) on the bedrock-runtime endpoint, with support for the Responses, Converse, and Chat Completions APIs in AWS GovCloud (US). It also adds support for Cross-Region Inference, allowing customers to use Cross-Region Inference within AWS GovCloud (US) regions to access higher throughput and increased redundancy.    
 Cross-Region Inference automatically routes inference requests across both AWS GovCloud (US) Regions to give you higher throughput, without you needing to manage capacity across multiple Regions. Cross-Region Inference within AWS GovCloud (US) routes requests across both regions so you can scale while maintaining US data sovereignty, giving you the broadest access to Bedrock capacity and the highest throughput during demand spikes. This launch also expands API support; you can use OpenAI GPT models with the Responses API, Chat Completions API, and the Converse API on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. Because these native OpenAI APIs now run on bedrock-runtime, the models work with the same account-level controls you already use for other models on Bedrock: usage appears in Bedrock model invocation l

title: Web Search now available on Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US)
body:
Kiro web search gives the agent real-time access to current information on the internet, so its answers draw on up-to-date search results and page content. The agent uses web search automatically when a question involves recent changes or topics beyond the model's training data. Answers that use web results include citations.  
 Kiro enterprise administrators can turn off web search and web fetch for their organization from the Kiro console under Settings. Teams can also remove web tools from individual custom agents, or block them with capability-based permission rules.  
 For more details, visit the  AWS GovCloud (US) documentation , the  monitoring and tracking guide , or contact your AWS account team. To learn more about Kiro, visit the  Kiro product page .

title: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts
body: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts, helping agents resume work without losing progress when connectivity is interrupted or when their browser is accidentally closed or refreshed. When agents return, their drafts are restored with the message body, recipients, subject line, and attachment references intact. Customers can also access saved draft data in their Amazon S3 buckets to build integrations with other applications.

title: Daybreak Red from OpenAI now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-East)
Amazon CloudFront now provides viewer ISP and post-quantum TLS details
body:
Amazon CloudFront can now forward two new optional headers to your origin. The CloudFront-Viewer-ISP header contains the name of the viewer's internet service provider (ISP), so you can see which network a request came from. The CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details header describes the cryptography used on each viewer's TLS connection, so you can see whether a connection used post-quantum cryptography (PQC).  
 With CloudFront-Viewer-ISP, you can break down traffic and performance by network. You can also isolate unusual traffic from a single provider. CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details includes the key exchange, signature scheme, and signature public key type for each connection. You can use it to measure the share of viewers that actually connect with PQC and identify clients that do not yet do so. To forward either header to your origin, add it to an origin request policy and attach the policy to your distribution.  
 To get started, see  adding CloudFront headers  and  controlling origin requests with a policy  in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide

title: Amazon MSK now supports TLS 1.3 for data in transit
body:
Amazon MSK now supports version 1.3 of Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol for MSK Provisioned clusters through encryption policies. TLS 1.3 delivers faster, more secure encryption for streaming data and is increasingly required by compliance frameworks and enterprise security standards. It is also one of the prerequisites for post-quantum cryptography for protecting data against attacks that collect encrypted traffic now with the intent to decrypt it later.  
 Customers can opt in to TLS 1.3 by selecting a named security policy in their MSK cluster configuration, with no change to existing clusters until a policy is applied. A named security policy defines which TLS version and cipher suites a cluster can accept. With this launch, Amazon MSK provides a set of policies customers can select and any connection that does not meet the selected policy requirements is rejected. This allows customers to stay in control of their security and compliance posture. Policies that support both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 allow connections to negotiate the highest version the client supports allowing clients that support TLS 1.3 to connect on it immediately while clients on TLS 1.2 continue to connec

title: Amazon RDS for Oracle no longer requires automatic minor version upgrades for JVM, Spatial, Locator, and OLAP options
body:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle  now lets you turn off automatic minor version upgrades on new and existing DB instances that use the JVM, Spatial, Locator, or OLAP option. Previously, these options required automatic minor version upgrades to be enabled.  
 With this change, you decide when to apply minor version upgrades to DB instances using these options. If you turn off automatic minor version upgrades, we recommend that you apply new minor versions regularly so your DB instances keep the latest Oracle security fixes. To keep automatic minor version upgrades turned on and still control the order in which your environments are upgraded, you can use  AWS Organizations upgrade rollout policy .  
 This change is available in  all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions  where Amazon RDS for Oracle is available. To learn more about options available in Amazon RDS for Oracle, see  Adding options to Oracle DB instances  in the Amazon RDS User Guide.

title: AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions
body: AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions. When you enable it, CloudFront adds the script tag for the AWS WAF JavaScript SDK to the HTML it serves, with no change to your application code, build process, or deployment. The SDK supplies the client-side signals used by three AWS WAF managed rule groups: Bot Control at the targeted inspection level, Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP), and Fraud Control account creation fraud prevention (ACFP).    Previously, supplying those signals required you to add a script tag to every page of every application you wanted to protect, and to maintain that tag across releases. For teams running many applications, or serving pages produced by systems they do not control, this created recurring work and a common source of misconfiguration, where a protection was enabled in AWS WAF but the client-side integration was missing. Enabling automatic SDK integration on the web ACL protecting your CloudFront distribution removes that per-application work.    Automatic SDK integration is available for web ACLs that are used with Amazon CloudFront and contain at least one of those managed rule groups. You can c

title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows
body:
Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows and flow modules, simplifying how you build, test, and deploy customer experience flows while minimizing impact to live end-customer traffic. With this launch, you can now create immutable versions of a flow and attach one or more friendly names (i.e., aliases) to a version, then point resources such as queues, quick connects, and phone numbers at an alias instead of a specific version.  
 Rolling out a new version takes a single update, with no need to republish or relink each resource. For example, you can publish an updated customer experience flow as a new version and validate it in a test environment while live traffic stays on the current version, then repoint the production alias to move every phone number to the new version in a single update.  
 This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. To learn more, see  Flow versioning and aliasing  in the Amazon Connect Customer Administrator Guide. To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the  Amazon Connect Customer website

title: Amazon Quick Introduces Quick Essentials
body:
Amazon Quick introduces Quick Essentials for enterprises. The plan makes it easier for organizations to get started with all the features of Quick such as AI-powered chat, Research, Flows, and Apps, and lets users view and interact with Quick Sight dashboards and reports and then manage adoption at the desired pace.  
 In AWS Regions where Amazon Quick is available, Quick Sight Reader users are upgraded to Quick Essentials at no additional per-user cost. With Quick Essentials, Quick Sight Readers can ask their dashboards questions in plain language, like what drove a revenue dip in March, and dig into the details with follow-up questions. They can turn the answer into a document, presentation, or spreadsheet for their team. When they need more context, Research pulls from their data, files, and the web into a detailed report with citations. If they need the same update every week, Flows can build it and send it automatically. When they need a tool that doesn't exist yet, like a request tracker, they can describe it and Apps builds it, without writing code.  
 Existing dashboards, Favorites, and Recents stay in place. Row-level and column-level security apply to every answer, and da

title: Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics
body:
Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics for  Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus  and  Amazon CloudWatch . The integration collects Kafka exporter metrics and consumer-group lag metrics from your Amazon MSK clusters. 
 Managed Prometheus collectors discover and collect Prometheus metrics from your workloads, so you don't run and operate collection agents yourself. You ingest the collected metrics into an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace or into Amazon CloudWatch, where you query and analyze them. You monitor Kafka stream health and consumer performance with consumer-group metrics. This helps you detect processing bottlenecks in your streaming applications. 
 This feature is available in all  AWS Regions  where managed Prometheus collectors are generally available. To learn more, see the documentation for  Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus  and  Amazon CloudWatch .

title: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning for real-time endpoints
body:
Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning, enabling you to run several models on a single GPU instead of dedicating a whole accelerator to each one. Using NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, SageMaker AI divides a GPU into as many as seven isolated partitions, each with its own memory and compute. Customers serving small and mid-size models, such as fine-tuned variants, embedding models, rerankers, and classifiers, previously had to give every model an entire accelerator, so an instance hosted no more models than it had GPUs and paid for GPU capacity those models could never use. 
 With GPU partitioning, you choose how to divide the GPUs behind your endpoint and place each model on a partition sized to fit it. Several models then share one accelerator with hardware-enforced isolation, so a busy model cannot take memory or throughput from the models beside it. Right-sizing an accelerator to a workload also opens up newer instance generations that would otherwise be more capacity than a single model needs. You configure GPU partitioning when you create an endpoint that hosts inference components, and you continue to invoke each model by name, so your applica

title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports Apache Iceberg table optimization in the US West (N. California) Region
body:
AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports automatic table optimization for Apache Iceberg tables in the US West (N. California) Region. Apache Iceberg is an open table format that delivers fast query performance over large tables in data lakes. With this launch, you can enable table optimization for individual tables or for all tables in your Data Catalog.  
 Apache Iceberg tables accumulate small files, snapshots, and unreferenced files with every write, which slows queries and increases storage costs over time. Table optimization continuously monitors your tables to compact small files in the background, remove snapshots that are past your retention settings, and delete unreferenced files that are no longer needed. You can monitor each run from the AWS Glue console, Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and logs.  
 You can enable table optimization using the AWS Glue console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. For the full list of Regions where table optimization is available, see  Supported Regions for table optimizers . To learn more, see  Optimizing Iceberg tables  in the AWS Glue Developer Guide. To get started, visit the  AWS Glue product page .

title: AWS Marketplace now enables partners to list once and sell through multiple subsidiary accounts
body:
Today, AWS announces that AWS partners who operate multiple legal entities can publish a product listing once in their primary account and enable their local subsidiaries to sell it through direct private offers — eliminating the need to recreate and maintain duplicate listings across every account.  
 From the primary account, which retains ownership of the listing, partners authorize which products each subsidiary can sell and which buyer countries it can extend private offers to. Each subsidiary transacts under its own local tax identity, selects the local currencies it supports, and sets its own disbursement preferences and bank account. The AWS Marketplace insights report in the primary account provides a consolidated view of offers, agreements, and renewals across all connected subsidiary accounts. Partners can revoke a subsidiary authorization or a subsidiary connection at any time, which immediately stops that subsidiary from creating new offers — agreements and offers already extended to buyers remain unchanged.  
 This capability is available today at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available. To get started, see   Managing subsidiary a

title: Amazon RDS for Oracle and SQL Server now support storage autoscaling on additional storage volumes
body:
Amazon RDS for SQL Server   and   Amazon RDS for Oracle   now support RDS storage autoscaling on  additional storage volumes . RDS storage autoscaling automatically scales storage capacity in response to growing database workloads, with zero downtime.  
 Additional storage volumes allow you to add up to three additional volumes to increase your storage capacity up to 256 TiB. Previously, you had to manually provision storage capacity on the additional storage volumes based on anticipated application capacity demands while autoscaling could be enabled on the primary storage volume. Under-provisioning could result in application downtime, and over-provisioning could result in under-utilized resources and higher costs. With RDS storage autoscaling, you simply set your desired maximum storage limit for each additional storage volume, and autoscaling takes care of the rest.  
 RDS storage autoscaling continuously monitors actual storage consumption, and scales capacity up automatically when actual utilization approaches provisioned storage capacity. Autoscaling works with new and existing database instances. Autoscaling has no additional charges and you only pay for the provisioned

title: Amazon Aurora now supports post-quantum TLS key exchange
body:
Starting today,  Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition  introduces support for post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange, providing you with post-quantum cryptography options for encrypting your data in transit.  
 Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL versions 18 and higher support modification of the ssl_groups parameter. You can  select cryptographic groups  from the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL allow list to align with your organization's security standards.  
 Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full PostgreSQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at our  getting started page .

title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports updating connector plugins and worker configurations
body:
Amazon MSK Connect   (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now lets you update the custom plugin and worker configuration of an existing connector. This is useful when you need to update the custom plugin to run a new version of your connector code, for example one with updated dependencies. You can also update the worker configuration to change worker-level settings, such as switching key and value converters or tuning producer and consumer properties for throughput and latency.  
 Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with   Amazon MSK   (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, updating a connector's plugin or worker configuration meant deleting the connector and recreating it - a disruptive operation that added risk and operational overhead. With this launch, you can update a connector's plugin and worker configuration in place. The connector keeps its committed offsets, so its tasks continue processing from where they left off once the update completes.  
 This capability is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Connect is supported. To lear

title: AWS Step Functions workflows now available as AI agent tools
body:
You can now use your AWS Step Functions workflows as tools for AI agents through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. Your agent decides when to run a workflow and what input to pass, and Step Functions runs each step exactly as you defined it. Agents can use your existing Standard and Express workflows as tools. 
 AWS Step Functions is a visual workflow service capable of orchestrating over 220 AWS services to help customers build distributed applications at scale. AgentCore Gateway connects AI agents to tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). With this launch, your agents can run multi-step business processes in the same order every time. For example, a customer support agent can start your refund workflow, and Step Functions runs the eligibility check, manager approval, and credit steps, so every refund follows your policy. Agents can also look up workflow runs, so an operations agent can tell your on-call engineer which order runs failed overnight and where, letting them go straight to fixing the step that broke. 
 This capability is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway is available. You pay standard rates for Step Functions and AgentCore Gat

title: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in additional Regions
body:
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in two additional AWS Regions: Canada (Central) and Africa (Cape Town). DAX is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for Amazon DynamoDB that delivers up to ten times performance improvement, from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds, even at millions of requests per second.  
 With DAX, you can accelerate read-intensive and bursty workloads such as real-time bidding, gaming leaderboards, and retail product catalogs, while offloading read traffic from your DynamoDB tables. DAX is API-compatible with DynamoDB, so you can add microsecond-latency caching to your applications with minimal code changes. Customers can now keep cached data within the Region and meet low-latency requirements while benefiting from a fully managed service, including automated patching and failover.  
 To learn more, see the  Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator page . For the full list of Regions where DAX is available, see the  AWS Regional Services page .

title: ACM now supports ACME for public certificates in AWS GovCloud (US)
body:
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) ACME protocol support is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West), providing a fully managed ACME server endpoint that issues public TLS certificates from Amazon Trust Services using any ACMEv2-compatible client, including Certbot, cert-manager for Kubernetes, and acme.sh. With the CA/Browser Forum mandating 47-day certificate lifetimes by 2029, manual management of public certificates becomes untenable. ACME support in ACM gives developers a standards-based path to fully automate certificate issuance and renewal. 
 To learn more, visit the  AWS News blog post , the  ACM ACME documentation , the  ACM pricing page , and the  AWS Regional Services page .

title: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, FSx for NetApp ONTAP, and Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization
body:
AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for Windows File Server and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP as source or destination locations. You can now run Windows to Windows transfers, such as from an on-premises file server to FSx for Windows File Server. Additionally, Enhanced mode agents can now run on Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization version 4.20 or later.  
 With this launch, you can use the same location options in Enhanced mode as in Basic mode. Enhanced mode processes data in parallel for higher performance, removes file count limitations, and provides detailed data transfer metrics. OpenShift Virtualization expands your agent deployment options alongside VMware ESXi, KVM, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Amazon EC2.  
 You can get started by choosing Enhanced mode when you create a task in the  AWS DataSync console . These capabilities are available in all AWS Regions where DataSync Enhanced mode is supported. To learn more, visit the  AWS DataSync documentation .

title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports SOCI-indexed images to start training jobs in seconds
body:
Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces support for Seekable OCI (SOCI)-indexed container images for training and processing jobs, so your jobs start running your code sooner. SOCI-indexed images start Amazon SageMaker AI training containers in seconds, cutting GPU idle time during image pulls by up to 90%, with no impact on training performance. Before a training or processing job can run, SageMaker AI downloads its container image to the instance. For deep learning images, which routinely exceed 10 GB, that download adds minutes to the start of every job, and you pay for that time. Now, when your image includes a SOCI index, SageMaker AI lazy-loads the image, fetching only the files needed to start the container and streaming the rest in the background as your code runs.  
 To use this feature, reference a SOCI-indexed image from a private Amazon ECR repository in your training or processing job. You can use a pre-indexed AWS Deep Learning Container by changing the image tag to its -soci variant, or add a SOCI index to your own image in Amazon ECR with open-source tools, without rebuilding the image. No changes to your job definition, entry point, or data channels are needed. SageMa

title: Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade to Grafana version 13.2
body:
Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade from Grafana version 12.4 to 13.2. Upgrading to version 13.2 brings features launched as part of open-source Grafana versions 13.0 to 13.2. These include Git Sync for dashboards, dynamic dashboards, and PromQL query support in the Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin. 
 With Git Sync, you can treat dashboards as code by linking a workspace to a Git repository. Dashboard modifications can be tracked, reviewed, and reverted through version control. Dynamic dashboards bring a more adaptable approach to layout and paneling. You can construct responsive views driven by conditions that respond to the data and variables in scope. With Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin support for Prometheus Query Language, you can use PromQL to query metrics that CloudWatch takes in via its OpenTelemetry (OTLP) endpoint, in addition to the existing Metric Search and Metrics Insights query types. 
 In-place upgrade to Grafana 13.2 is supported in all  AWS regions  where Amazon Managed Grafana is generally available. You can upgrade with just a few clicks from the AWS Console, AWS SDK or AWS CLI. For a complete list of new features, refer to  Differenc

title: Amazon Redshift announces hands-off automated cross-region backups
body:
Amazon Redshift  announces automated cross-region snapshot copy for Amazon Redshift. You can now have your Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster or serverless workgroup automatically backed up to the target AWS region(s) you choose. The automated cross-region snapshot copy feature will automatically, always copy the most recent snapshot with no manual intervention, continuously and incrementally and ensure your cluster is backed-up to the destination region(s), giving you additional options for business continuity.  
 The benefit to enabling the new automated cross-region snapshot copy feature is that you do not need to manually intervene to initiate a cross-region snapshot copy when an unplanned outage event occurs. Also, this feature takes the most recent snapshot available on your system to copy to the destination region, so you don't have to wait for the next snapshot to be taken, making it independent of your snapshot schedule on your local cluster. To configure cross-region snapshot copy, you need to enable the automated cross-region snapshot copy feature for each cluster and configure the destination region(s) to copy snapshots and how long to keep copied automated snapshots i

title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations
body:
Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations, named permission sets that control what actions individual project members can perform. Previously, project members could only be assigned Owner or Contributor designations, which provided nearly identical permissions. With custom designations, administrators define permission sets that align with their organization's personas and assign them to project members. Designations govern all actions within a project, providing administrators with a single permission model for separation of duties. 
 Administrators create designations in the SageMaker Unified Studio administration portal by selecting permissions grouped into categories such as Catalog, Subscriptions, Connections, Notebooks, and Data Agent. For example, a "Data Steward" designation might include permissions to approve subscription requests and publish assets, while an "Analyst" designation is limited to querying data and running notebooks. Each designation is defined at the domain level and assigned across any project in that domain. When a member performs an action, SageMaker Unified Studio evaluates their assigned designation and permits or denies the requ

title: AWS Backup now supports cross-account management and cross-account backup in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud
body:
AWS Backup now supports cross-account management, cross-account backup, and delegated administrators in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. These capabilities help you centrally manage, monitor, and copy backups across the accounts in your organization using AWS Organizations.  
 With cross-account management, you can deploy organization-wide backup policies from your AWS Organizations management account or a delegated administrator account. You can also monitor backup, copy, and restore jobs across all of your organization accounts from one place. With cross-account backup, you can copy recovery points to a backup vault in another account in your organization, which adds protection against accidental or malicious deletion in the source account. You can also register a member account as a delegated administrator, so your teams can manage backups across your organization without needing access to your management account.  
 There is no additional charge to use these capabilities; standard AWS Backup pricing applies. To learn more, see the AWS Backup documentation at  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/ . To get started, visit the AWS Backup console at  https://con

title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports September 2026 Monthly Recommended Patch
body:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle  now supports the September 2026 Monthly Recommended Patch (MRP) for Oracle Database version 19c and 26ai. An MRP is a minor engine version that builds on a quarterly Release Update (RU), bundling Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update (CSPU) with additional Oracle-recommended fixes. The September 2026 MRP is applied on top of the July 2026 RU and includes the  Oracle September CSPU . We recommend upgrading to the September 2026 MRP as it includes the latest security updates for Oracle Database.  
 This release also includes the updated Oracle time zone file (DST version 46), which reflects the latest daylight saving time rule changes in several regions, including British Columbia and Alberta in Canada (effective November 1, 2026) and Morocco and Western Sahara (effective September 20, 2026), which are moving to permanent UTC offsets. If you store timestamps that include time zone information for these areas, the updated time zone file keeps that data aligned with the new rules.  
 You can apply the September 2026 MRP for new database instances, or upgrade existing instances to engine version 19.0.0.0.ru-2026-07.mrp-2026-0

body:
AWS announces the general availability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI version 1.0 (@aws/agentcore 1.0.0), rebuilt with faster startup, a consistent command structure, and support for more AgentCore resources. The CLI helps developers create, develop, deploy, and operate AI agents and supporting resources from the terminal.  
 With version 1.0, developers can use the project workflow or work directly with harnesses, runtimes, memory, identity, gateways, and payments without first adding them to a project. Developers can invoke existing resources by ID or ARN, open an interactive shell, export a harness, and use searchable menus, resource pickers, and guided workflows. Consistent global flags provide region selection, JSON output, debugging, and version information across commands.  
 Existing projects can be migrated to AgentCore version 1 using the agentcore migrate command.  
 Install AgentCore CLI version 1.0 from  npm  or explore the source on  GitHub . To learn more, visit the  Amazon Bedrock AgentCore product page ,  AgentCore CLI reference , and  Get started with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore .

Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports public endpoints in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. A public endpoint lets you connect to your cache from a serverless function or any application running outside a VPC, without setting up a VPN, a bastion host, or an SSH tunnel.  
 With a public endpoint, ElastiCache Serverless gives you a fully managed cache with no VPC to configure and no infrastructure to provision, and you can create one in under a minute. Every connection uses IAM authentication over TLS 1.3, so there's no password to store or rotate. Connect using Valkey GLIDE 2.2 or later, which has built-in IAM support, or another Valkey client paired with the Developer Toolkit for ElastiCache, an open-source library that generates and refreshes IAM authentication tokens for you.  
 With this expansion, public endpoints for ElastiCache Serverless are now available in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the China Regions. There is no additional charge for using public endpoints beyond standard ElastiCache Serverless pricing.

title: AWS Lambda supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) lazy loading for Lambda Managed Instances
body:
AWS Lambda now supports  Seekable OCI (SOCI)  for lazy loading  Event Functions  packaged as Open Container Initiative (OCI) images running on  Lambda Managed Instances . With SOCI support, Lambda fetches only the files needed at each stage of the execution environment startup rather than downloading the entire image upfront, reducing container startup times by up to 70%.  
 Customers building compute-intensive applications such as data processing pipelines, high-throughput API backends, and batch computation workloads require substantial memory and CPU resources to process large datasets, serve low-latency responses at scale, and run complex computations efficiently. Container images for these workloads can reach several gigabytes, and downloading and preparing the full image can take several minutes when provisioning new execution environments. SOCI support on Lambda Managed Instances eliminates this bottleneck by streaming only the required files at each stage of the execution environment startup, so your functions start faster as you scale.

body:
Today, we're announcing support for time series collections on the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless. With time series collections, you can ingest, store, and analyze logs, metrics, traces, and event data without provisioning or managing clusters. They absorb ingest spikes automatically, keep recent data fast to query, and make months or years of history searchable at low cost, all in the same collection.  
 Time series collections add a new, lower-cost warm storage tier in addition to the existing hot storage tier, so customers can retain their infrequently accessed data without paying hot storage prices. Customers can choose how long data stays hot before transitiong to warm storage.  With up to 100 TB of hot storage per collection, time series collections can handle high-volume observability workloads such as application monitoring, security analytics, and IoT telemetry. Alerting and anomaly detection are also now available, so customers can get notified about issues and spot unusual patterns in their log and event data without separate tooling.

title: Quick now supports smart approvals for agentic actions
body:
Amazon Quick now supports smart approvals, a review layer that reduces unnecessary approval prompts while preserving human oversight of the actions that matter most. As agents take more actions on a user's behalf, such as sending email, updating records, and creating tickets, asking a person to approve every step leads to approval fatigue and weaker oversight over time. With smart approvals, a separate review model called the classifier evaluates each eligible action against the user's request. It approves routine actions automatically and refers consequential actions to the user for review.  
 Your existing policies always come first. Smart approvals only reviews actions where the user's setting is "ask" each time. Denied actions stay denied, and smart approvals never grants new access. The classifier sends higher-impact actions to the user for review. These include sending content outside the organization, changing permissions, deleting content, making payments, and actions that go beyond what the user asked for. Each automatic approval covers only the exact action that was reviewed. If a review fails or times out, the action goes to the user.  
 Smart approvals is on for all use

The Amazon EKS Dashboard already provides centralized visibility into your clusters across AWS Regions and accounts, and it now includes CA rotation, so you can see where action is needed without checking each cluster individually.  
 Each Amazon EKS cluster has its own CA, and clusters created since 2018 have CAs with a 10-year validity period that are now approaching the point where rotation activities should begin. In the EKS Dashboard, you can now see your clusters and their CA rotation status, which clusters have CAs approaching expiration, and upcoming automated rotation events, so platform teams who operate many clusters can prioritize action across their fleet from one place.  
 The Amazon EKS Dashboard aggregates data across your accounts and Regions through AWS Organizations, so you enable trusted access for the dashboard in your organization’s management account to use this capability. You view the dashboard from the US East region (us-east-1), and it is available at

title: Amazon ECS Managed Instances adds cross-instance and Spot consolidation
body:
Today,  Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Managed Instances  introduces two infrastructure optimization updates: cross-instance and Spot consolidation. Cross-instance consolidation evaluates tasks running across multiple underutilized instances together, packing them onto fewer instances to raise utilization and lower costs. Spot consolidation extends this capability to Spot capacity, consolidating underutilized Spot Instances after first verifying replacement capacity is available. 
 Amazon ECS Managed Instances provisions, configures, and operates right-sized Amazon EC2 instances for your workloads, balancing availability and cost. Its infrastructure optimization continuously monitors your fleet, reclaiming idle capacity and consolidating underutilized instances with graceful start-before-stop task replacement. Until now, optimization evaluated each instance in isolation for replacement, which worked well when a capacity provider was configured with diverse instance types. However, when a capacity provider was configured with a narrow range of instance types, there were fewer opportunities to consolidate multiple underutilized instances, because no single replacement

title: AWS Lambda durable functions now exports live telemetry for execution insights
body:

This new observability plugin captures the step-by-step history of your durable executions and sends them to one or more destinations of your choice. You can use the exported data to gather operational and business insights and keep history beyond the standard retention period. We are also releasing a companion Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents such as Kiro query your exported telemetry data using natural language.  
 Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year. The new Telemetry Exporter sends data such as execution status, operation timing, step input and output, and errors to 13 built-in destinations. Destinations include Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3 for Amazon Athena, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Aurora, and Amazon OpenSearch Service. You can redact sensitive fields before export and set a sampling rate to control data volume. title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports Kubernetes Gateway API
body:
Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports the Kubernetes Gateway API, giving customers a standard, portable way to define how traffic reaches their applications. Customers can configure application load balancing using Gateway and HTTPRoute resources, and EKS Auto Mode provisions and manages the underlying AWS infrastructure automatically.  
 With this launch, EKS Auto Mode customers can adopt the next-generation Kubernetes traffic management standard without installing or configuring a separate controller. Capabilities include HTTP and gRPC routing, cross-namespace traffic routing for multi-team environments, weighted traffic splitting, header-based routing, and automatic TLS certificate discovery through AWS Certificate Manager. Existing workloads using Ingress resources continue to work alongside Gateway API resources.  
 To get started, see the  Amazon EKS documentation . Gateway API support is included as part of EKS Auto Mode and is available in all AWS Regions where EKS Auto Mode is supported. Standard charges apply for the AWS load balancing resources provisioned.

title: AWS Backup adds restore testing support for Amazon Redshift
body:
AWS Backup restore testing now supports Amazon Redshift. Restore testing helps you automate and periodically run restore tests of your backups, so you can confirm that your Amazon Redshift backups restore successfully and measure how long the restores take.  
 You can now include Amazon Redshift in your restore testing plans alongside other supported AWS resources across storage, compute, and database services. Restore testing plans automatically select recovery points, run restores on a schedule, and measure restore job completion time against your recovery time objectives (RTO). This helps you evaluate recovery readiness and meet regulatory and compliance requirements for disaster recovery and business continuity.  
 To get started, create a restore testing plan and assign your Amazon Redshift resources by Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or tag. Choose whether each test restores the latest or a random eligible recovery point. Optionally, use restore testing validation to confirm the restored resource before AWS Backup deletes the test resources.

With AWS Agent Registry, you can publish MCP servers, tools, agents, agent skills, and custom resources into a searchable registry, control access through an approval workflow, and enable both human users and AI agents to discover the right tools and agents through hybrid search, catalog browsing, and a native MCP endpoint.

title: AWS IAM Identity Center's Identity Store now supports change notifications through Amazon EventBridge
body:
AWS IAM Identity Center's Identity Store now delivers real-time events to Amazon EventBridge when users, groups, or group memberships or the identity store itself is created, updated, or deleted. AWS IAM Identity Center Identity Store is a central repository that allows you to manage identities and access across AWS accounts and applications, serving as the identity source for AWS IAM Identity Center. This new capability helps you automatically respond to identity lifecycle events and support your security and compliance processes by detecting changes as they happen.  
 With Identity Store change notifications, you can build automated workflows that respond to identity changes in your organization. For example, security teams can create EventBridge rules that trigger AWS Lambda functions to audit user provisioning activity, send alerts to security information and event management (SIEM) systems, or update access in downstream applications when users or groups change. Organizations that manage large workforces can also use this data to automate onboarding and offboarding when users are added to or removed from specific groups.  
 Change notifications are available in all AWS Regions

title: Postal Service Surveilled Protest Activities Online With Little Rules, Oversight
body:
The U.S. Postal Service used social media surveillance to monitor and report on protests across the political spectrum, government records show. 
 The  records , disclosed to EFF and other requesters suing the postal service under the Freedom of Information Act, show that the agency’s internet Covert Operations Program, or iCOP, routinely sifted through social media posts organizing and discussing protests with little records of any oversight or legal justification. 
 EFF filed  suit in 2021  after  Yahoo News  disclosed the program’s existence and how the agency used it to monitor First Amendment protected activities. After years of delays and technical failures that led the agency to lose access to a trove of emails discussing the program, the postal service disclosed records to EFF and several other requesters this year. 
  The Postal Service used iCOP to surveil First Amendment activities  
 The disclosures include a series of bulletins created from iCOP, which show that the postal service used the program in 2020 and 2021 to monitor and circulate information about a wide range of planned protests. They included a planned “ Million MAGA March ,” a  guns rights advocacy  event a

title: Privacy's Defenders Podcast: The Secret Room
body:
The government’s surveillance powers grew rapidly after Sept. 11, 2001, some in public view and some in secret. EFF suspected but couldn’t prove that the National Security Agency was spying on Americans' communications. The New York Times sat on a story about it for over a year, finally publishing it in December 2005. Then, in January 2006, a retired AT&T technician named    Mark Klein    walked into EFF's office with a manila folder of documents that blew the story wide open.     
  Welcome to the third episode of “Privacy’s Defenders,” a podcast about the people – lawyers, journalists, hackers, and others – who’ve fought to secure your digital liberties since before most people even knew what the internet was.

title: Independent Digital Media Is Not a Privilege Governments Can Revoke: The Fight to Save Egypt’s Mada Masr
body:
On November 11, Lina Attalah, founder and editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet    Mada Masr   , will face trial for the second time in just two weeks. This time, she faces charges of spreading false news, an accusation that has become one of the Egyptian government's most frequently used tools for prosecuting journalists.     
  The trial follows a conviction on October 27, when Attalah was    found guilty    of managing an unlicensed news website. The Mada Masr team had repeatedly applied for a license, but their attempts went unacknowledged. The proceedings took place in a single hearing, which Mada Masr    states    included serious violations of her right to a fair trial. She was sentenced to the maximum fine of 3 million Egyptian pounds (approximately 55,000 USD), forcibly removed from the courtroom, and held for seven hours until the fine was paid. The court also ordered Mada Masr's closure and the confiscation of all equipment belonging to the organization.

It’s easy to see these cases as a David-and-Goliath showdown between authors and publishers fighting for a cut of Big Tech company profits. But this fight is actually much larger. It affects billions of people who aren’t represented in the case at all, including researchers, artists, activists, journalists, people with disabilities, and anyone who accesses and shares content online.    
 That’s why EFF is stepping in to defend the  public’s  rights in these cases. Today, EFF filed an  amicus brief  in  In re OpenAI,  explaining how the court’s ruling on fair use could impact people worldwide. If fair use gets narrowed, it will impede work that benefits the public, like medical research and investigative journalism, and even limit access to privacy protection tools.

title: Why VPNs Are Worth Defending
body:
Developers of  virtual private network (VPN)  apps are  reporting  that their products are again being pulled from Apple’s App Store in Russia. This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online. 
 Why? VPNs give people a way to control their own online activities. When you visit a website through a VPN, that website only sees the VPN server's location (well, IP address) rather than your actual location. It's like sending a letter through a P.O. box so the recipient doesn't know where you really live. It can also disguise where you’re accessing information from,  which can make it possible  to access information banned by your government. 
 This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online. 
 Going after tools that give people the space to communicate and access information freely is a common tactic from the totalitarian playbook. This latest demand comes after several steps the Russian government’s taken to surveil speech specifically on Apple products. title: Tech Tips for Parents this Digital Parenting Week
body:
In today’s digital world, the internet is an    essential resource    for young people to access information, explore community, and find themselves. But we know that this often comes alongside fears of experiencing online harms like doxxing, grooming, or bullying.  
  Trying to protect your family from everything all the time is impractical and exhausting, but some thoughtful planning can help families devise a workable plan that meets their needs and addresses their concerns.  
  That’s why this Digital Parent Week, we’re sharing easy tips on how parents and their children can work together to co-curate a digital safety plan that helps all members of the family enjoy the benefits of technology while protecting their online privacy and safety.   
  Start with Open Conversations  
  Online safety begins with communication, not just restrictions. Talk with a young person about how they use the internet: their favourite apps, games, and social media platforms for example. title: Victory! You Can Now Exclude Apps from Siri AI
body:
In the most recent update to Apple’s devices, iOS 27.2, the company has introduced a new setting to “Exclude Apps” from Siri AI, fulfilling one of our asks from    our Encrypt It Already campaign earlier this year   .  
  One of our main concerns with new AI features on devices is how those features interact with end-to-end encrypted content, particularly with secure messaging apps. Many AI features require cloud processing, and despite    privacy protections engineered into these systems   , the content of secure messaging apps may leave a user’s device without their knowledge. That changes the privacy concerns around using those tools. In a perfect world, users would be able to put a barrier up to ensure data from certain apps doesn’t leave the device. Here was our initial ask:  
   You should be able to tell the operating system’s AI to not access an app, even if that comes at the “cost” of missing out on some features. The setting should be straightforward and easy to understand in ways the Gemini and Apple Intelligence controls currently are not.

title: Court Should Curb Abuse of Grand Jury Subpoenas Targeting Social Media Users
body:
A federal appeals court should curb the government’s abuse of grand jury subpoenas to unmask social media users who criticize lawless immigration enforcement. 
 That is the message from the ACLU, EFF, and other civil liberties and trade groups who filed  a friend-of-the-court brief  in a sealed case in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia. 
  The case involves  the government’s investigation of an anonymous Reddit user who commented on a post about an immigration officer in Minnesota. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) first issued an administrative subpoena to Reddit to unmask the user. When the user challenged the subpoena in court on free speech and statutory grounds ( as many others have ), DHS withdrew it. But then the government obtained a separate grand jury subpoena—a subpoena issued by a prosecutor to gather evidence to present to a grand jury before any criminal charges are filed—for much of the same information. The user then challenged the grand jury subpoena too, and the case is currently being appealed.

title: 💾 Fighting DOGE's Data Grab | EFFector 38.19
body:

title: Social Media When Elections Are Close: Doing the Impossible Better
body:
Everyone knows, or should, that perfect (balanced, targeted, transparent, swift and swiftly appealable) content moderation at scale is impossible. That doesn’t mean powerful social platforms don’t have to try to get at least reasonably close, especially when access to good information can have a profound effect on political participation and speech. 
 That’s why so many people, including the  Meta Oversight Board , criticized Meta for suspending a major  political Instagram account  for hours during a huge early voting push on October 17; and  for allegedly  boosting one candidate in Brazil’s recent presidential election. Meta denies deliberate interference in either instance, blaming  “mistakes”  in its automated content moderation systems (including AI tools that can’t tell the difference between enthusiastic follower engagement and a bot attack). 
 Mistakes or not, with early voting in the U.S. midterms already underway, these events serve as a stark reminder that all major social media platforms need to have stronger systems in place to ensure that they serve, rather than impede, democratic communication.

title: French Court’s Site-Blocking Orders Drive Quad9 Out Of France
body:
A nonprofit service that protects internet users’ privacy is leaving France. Quad9, a free DNS resolver, has said    it will reluctantly stop serving users in France    on November 24. This follows a French court order that Quad9 must block access to websites that are accused of infringing the copyrights of a sports broadcaster. Forcing a responsible privacy service out of an important market is a predictable result of trying to force infrastructure providers to be copyright police.  
  When you visit a website, a DNS resolver reads the domain name you type in—like    eff.org   — and translates it into a numerical IP address that’s used to direct data across the internet. A DNS resolver can see the names of websites you connect to, so its privacy policies are important. Quad9 is an NGO that’s incorporated in Switzerland, in part to protect its users from data demands. The company also helps protect users from malware and phishing by blocking domains that are known to be malicious. Services like Quad9 offer an alternative to the DNS resolvers of local internet service providers and wireless carriers, which are vulnerable to demands from law enforcement, censorship, and commercial su

title: Lessons Learned From 'AdFection' and What To Do Next
body:
Last week,    researchers at Citizen Lab revealed    a horrifying new malware campaign, dubbed “AdFection.” It used an ad network to distribute spyware to journalist’s devices to infect them without the target ever needing to click anything. This sort of attack on journalists is dangerous and incredibly concerning, especially since it’s built on the backbone of a technology we already object to:    behavioral advertising   . Although this type of attack has only been described targeting journalists, you can take a few steps we outline in the next section to mitigate the risk no matter who you are.  
  A few factors combined to make this attack a noteworthy first-of-its-kind. First, it utilized the surveillance ad-tech ecosystem to specially target the malicious code. Second, the spyware it delivered was so-called “zero-click,” meaning it required no interaction from the user to be infected: all that is required is for the ad to be delivered and code bundled along with it to be run, which happens automatically. title: Anti-Circumvention Laws Raise the Cost of Knowledge
body:
The vast amount of information on the open web requires researchers and journalists to adapt with new tools to make sense of it all. Checking facts, gauging public opinion, and other lines of inquiry depend on being able to analyze the overwhelming amount of material posted online every day. Unfortunately, responding to the AI industry’s voracious appetite for data, companies stewarding this public data are looking to cash in and block access to the open web. This makes the web harder to navigate, and threatens all kinds of important research. 
 Reddit’s  lawsuit  against SerpAPI[1] and Perplexity threatens to do exactly that. 
 Reddit was once a very open platform, fostering a community of alternative apps and extensions putting users in control of their experience. Since the rise of AI however, it changed tack. Over the last three years Reddit has  closed APIs to users , limited  UI features , and otherwise restrained access  without login . body:

You may find yourself wondering: what is PHP, what just happened, what is the vulnerability apocalypse, and what do I need to do?      
   To find out what you can personally do read the  first blog post  in this series!

  PHP is a programming language used mainly to create interactive websites. Facebook, Wordpress, Wikipedia, Etsy, and other major sites all use or were originally built on PHP. It is a long-established mainstay of web development. But because it is open-source, maintenance of these critical systems depends on a small number of volunteers working on this in their free time. The disaster scenario that happened this past week is the perfect example of why we need more money and people supporting open-source projects. title: Computer Security Is About to Get a Lot Worse, Here’s What You Can Do
body:
It is a commonly held truth among computer geeks that there is no such thing as bug-free software, or a secure computer. Any piece of software that anyone actually uses  will have a security vulnerability somewhere in the code . The more complex that software is, the more likely there will be a vulnerability. Fortunately for everyone, finding severe vulnerabilities was generally considered an expensive and difficult task requiring years of training and deep knowledge of how computers and software worked. Until recently there was a steady background hum of vulnerabilities being found and patched, with major vulnerabilities that could cripple the entire internet only happening every few years. Now that is no longer the case.      
  You may have noticed your nerdiest friends freaking out about the “Vulnerability Apocalypse” this week and waving their arms in panic about something called PHP. You may have also noticed that some of your favorite websites were down for a bit. title: Interoperability vs. Security: Why not both?
body:
An open internet where people can freely build, share, and remix each other's work is a powerful engine of grassroots innovation we’ve all benefited from. In recent decades, however, corporations have taken control of an increasing share of this work, giving them a greater ability to stifle challengers and limit our choices. When regulators address this by mandating that  tech giants play fair by requiring interoperability, the gatekeepers respond with a tired refrain: Playing fair puts users’ security at risk.  
  Unfortunately for these trillion-dollar companies, this     gotcha     isn’t the end of the conversation. Regulators can ensure that meaningful choice    and    security thrive.  
  Lawmakers have been catching up, recognizing that the best way to rein in big tech is to require these    oligopolies    to open up their platforms to independent developers. As we    explained six years ago   , mandating interoperability helps prevent the misuse of people’s data and enables more privacy-respecting alternatives. Tech giants, in contrast, have been arguing that our data is safer when they have exclusive control.

title: EFF to Brazil’s ANPD: Data Privacy and Free Expression Must Underpin Platform Regulations
body:
The Brazilian National Data Protection Agency (ANPD) plays a pivotal role in the regulation of digital platforms according to new legislation approved in Brazil. Throughout this year, EFF has presented comments, filed submissions, and met with the agency to emphasize crucial guardrails that the enforcement of new regulations should ensure.     
  ANPD is responsible for detailing and applying obligations set in Law n. 15.211/2025, which established rules for the protection of children and adolescents in the digital space. While some provisions establish important privacy safeguards, like prohibiting advertising based on profiling of underage users, the law created mandatory age assurance mechanisms for accessing digital products and services.

title: EFF’s State Legislative Agenda to End ALPR Mass Surveillance
body: Police agencies across the U.S. have deployed Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) to capture images of passing vehicles along with time, date, and GPS coordinates. While the technology itself isn’t new (ALPRs have existed in various forms for  more than 50 years , and in  the U.S. since 1998 ), the surveillance landscape has shifted dramatically. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence and national data sharing have transformed police ALPRs into an interconnected, nationwide tracking network. It is pitched to city councils by law enforcement and private vendors like Flock Safety, Motorola Solutions (Vigilant), and Axon as an essential tool for solving violent crime.  In reality, it is an inherently dangerous infrastructure of mass surveillance.  Since  2012 , EFF has worked with others to expose the severe digital rights harms of ALPR systems. For example, we’ve recently documented how these camera networks allow law enforcement to  search for immigrants ,  track peaceful protesters , target  Romani communities , and  track women seeking reproductive healthcare . title: Victory! Court Rules OPM Data Disclosure to DOGE Is Unlawful
body:
In a victory for data privacy,  a federal court in New York definitively ruled  that the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) violated the law when it disclosed millions of federal employee records to DOGE agents. In a summary judgment ruling issued on October 20, 2026, the court found that OPM violated two provisions of the Privacy Act—one restricting disclosure of personal records between agencies and another requiring agencies to protect the security and confidentiality of records. 
 Since the case was filed, many DOGE agents have left the government and OPM has rescinded their database access. However, OPM should still clean up the cybersecurity mess it created. The court will decide the remedy at a later date. 
 "By virtue of the Court’s summary judgment ruling, OPM’s decision to grant DOGE Agents broad access to its systems of recordings containing [personally identifiable information (PII)] has been held unlawful," Judge Denise Cote wrote. 
 "The record also provides no support for a finding that it was the pursuit of a modernization agenda that prompted OPM to grant sweeping and expedited access to a score of DOGE Agents to its systems of records containing PII," she added.

title: Require Police to Get a Warrant to Search ALPR Data
body:
This post was co-written by     Andi Cao    , an EFF legal intern.  
 Automated license plate readers (ALPRs) are mass surveillance. They photograph every passing car and log where and when it was captured, building a searchable record of where nearly everyone drives.   Cities should not buy them  , and cities that already have them should shut them down. 
 Where these systems still operate, courts and state legislatures must reduce their harms by (among other things) requiring police to get a warrant before searching stored ALPR data. A warrant requirement would not make mass surveillance acceptable, but it would require police to justify a search to a judge before accessing records of people’s movements. Without this independent judicial check on police power, officers have been searching this data for improper reasons (many exposed by EFF) that violate our fundamental rights. 
 A warrant requires a judge to find probable cause and specificity—many warrantless police searches of ALPR data lack both. title: In Memoriam: Barry Steinhardt
body:
Barry Steinhardt, a lifelong privacy champion and an early leader in the battle for digital civil liberties who served as EFF’s president in 1998-99, died last week at age 73.     
  A Connecticut native, Steinhardt led the Vermont and Pennsylvania affiliates of the American Civil Liberties Union before becoming associate director of the national ACLU. There, he helped spearhead the fight to overturn much of the Communications Decency Act, resulting in the U.S. Supreme Court’s landmark     Reno v. ACLU     ruling in 1997.     
  When the internet was still young,   Steinhardt   became one of   the first   attorneys to   specialize in the intersection of technology and privacy  .   In early 1998 he took a leave of absence from the ACLU to become EFF’s president, and then returned to the ACLU in 1999.     
  In 2002 he founded the ACLU’s Program on Technology and Liberty. After retiring from the ACLU, he continued on as a senior advisor to London-based  Privacy International .

title: The internet should not demand constant self-defence: Fairness starts before the click
body:
A fair digital environment cannot – and should not – depend on everyone being permanently alert. Fairness must be built into the environment itself, not left to the skills of the people using it. In practice, that means rules, not appeals: cancelling must be as easy as subscribing, protection must be the default rather than a setting, and a system that detects a moment of weakness must not be allowed to act on it.

title: What the new Convention on Decent Work in the Platform Economy means for workers – and what’s next for implementation
body:
In June 2026, the International Labour Organisation (ILO) adopted a new Convention on Decent Work in the Platform Economy. Following in the footsteps of the EU’s Platform Work Directive, this Convention extends data protection rights for platform workers and contains innovative provisions to protect against the adverse effects of automated decision-making globally. But this is only the beginning.  In this article, EDRi member Privacy International explores what’s next for ratification, implementation and the future of regulating worker surveillance in the EU and around the world.

title: Surveillance in times of insecurity: a wicked and stupid strategy
body:

The difficulty to address violent crimes in cities notably has triggered extensive legislative reforms to increase surveillance and repression, including that of children. title: CPDP 20th international conference
body:
CPDP (“Computers, Privacy and Data Protection”) is a non-profit platform founded in 2007 by research groups at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel, the Université de Namur, and Tilburg University, later joined by INRIA and the Fraunhofer Institute for Systems and Innovation Research. title: The Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) represents everything that’s wrong with Europe’s approach to digital sovereignty
body:
The EU’s Tech Sovereignty Package is supposed to jump-start Europe’s “sovereign AI” ambitions.  But due to fundamental misunderstandings about the technology behind ‘AI’ and the blind trust in Big Tech’s AI doomer and boomer narratives, it is more likely to instead hurt digital rights and the environment instead, and waste valuable public resources that should have been invested in actually increasing Europe’s digital resilience. The Cloud and AI Development (CADA) Act, a part of the Tech Sovereignty Package, adds up to an aggressive policy push to impose “European AI”.

body:

body:

title: The KIDS Act will make the internet less safe
body:
On 16 September, the European Commission presented the KIDS ACT, its plan for making online experiences safer for young people. Far from being a move to lead the EU towards better digital environments, this move is a missed opportunity to address the root cause of why online platforms are harmful to children – and everyone else. This blog analyse the proposal’s shortcomings.

title: Dinosaur Blood Found In Fossils For the First Time
body: Researchers have confirmed the presence of intact biomolecules and mineralized red blood cells inside the 115-million-year-old fossilized bones of a juvenile Aratasaurus museunacionali from Brazil. The discovery challenges assumptions about how long blood-related biomolecules can survive and could help scientists study dinosaur metabolism, blood evolution and even how traces of ancient life might be preserved on other worlds. Popular Science reports: The evidence exists inside the fossilized limb bones of a juvenile Aratasaurus museunacionali. Discovered in 2008, A. museunacionali was an Early Cretaceous theropod that lived in present-day northeastern Brazil. The fossils suggest a dinosaur measuring over 10 feet long and weighing about 75 pounds, but given its young age, A. museunacionali likely grew even larger. After carefully examining thin slices of the fossils, paleontologists located the mineralized red blood cell molecular components, along with a complex manganese oxide called hausmannite. This material helped maintain the cellular structures of heme, a ring-shaped molecule that contains iron and binds many proteins, especially hemoglobin. The hausmannite also helped preser

body:

Democrats flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats in the 2026 midterms, including surprise victories in traditionally Republican strongholds such as Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina. Kansas elected its first Democratic U.S. senator in nearly 100 years (94 years to be exact), while Texas and South Carolina sent Democrats to the Senate for the first time in decades. Democrats also picked up seats in Ohio, Iowa, Maine, and North Carolina.

title: Ubuntu plans firmware HWE to prevent issues on older kernels
body:
Ubuntu is planning a new linux-firmware-hwe package, in an effort to reduce the risk of firmware updates for newer kernels causing problems for users running older ones. On Ubuntu long-term support (LTS) releases, you can stick with the standard (GA) kernel it was released with for the duration of its support period, or you can install the HWE update, which brings newer Linux kernel versions to existing Ubuntu LTS releases.  Right now, both kernels share the same firmware package, which means firmware updates designed to work with HWE kernels can cause problems for users who stick with the GA kernel. title: Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet (Threat Intelligence)
body:
The Google Threat Intelligence blog  describes,
in great detail , the XCPE botnet, which has just been taken down.
 
 
	Last week, Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE
	backdoor which enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes into a
	botnet. We assess with high confidence that the backdoor and botnet
	were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial
	gain by Videostrong Technology Co., an Android Original Equipment
	Manufacturer (OEM) and Original Device Manufacturer (ODM).
 
	Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal
	affiliates and loading those affiliates' malware modules onto
	infected devices. These secondary modules were conducting ad-fraud;
	silently enrolling infected devices into residential proxy
	networks; and loading additional malware onto XCPE-compromised
	devices.

title: Kernel prepatch 7.4-rc1
body:
The  7.4-rc1  kernel prepatch is out, and
the merge window is closed for this development cycle.
 
 
	This is a *BIG* merge window. I think the reason is the by now
	obvious one, but I'm actually taking it as a good sign: I'm *much*
	happier with the flood of AI triggered work going into the merge
	window than it showing up mainly as extra fixes during the -rc
	period. So I'm hoping that this merge window being larger than
	usual is a sign that the AI fixes are becoming more part of the
	"normal development" than a flood of fixes that go into the whole
	stabilization phase. I think that's a much healthier model.
 
 
There were 18,591 non-merge changesets brought in during this merge window
— this is not just a record, but it nearly matches the patch volume during
the entire (record-setting) 7.3 development cycle.  So far, 2,678
developers have contributed to 7.4; 625 of them are first-time kernel
contributors.  Subscribers can find more details in  the KSDB 7.4 page .

title: How We Could Have Backdoored Bash (Hacktron blog)
body:
The Hacktron blog  documents  how
the group was able to compromise the GNU Savannah forge and could have
pushed malware into any of the projects hosted there.
 
 
	Using Hacktron, we found that an email address like
	 a`touch${IFS}/tmp/savane-rce-proof`@attacker.example  gave any
	registered user code execution on its backend. From there, we made
	our account a superuser, impersonated Bash's maintainer, and
	confirmed we could add an SSH key with push access to the upstream
	Bash repository. An unpatched kernel gave us root access and access
	to a GNU backup server. We reported it to the FSF on May 11, 2026.

title: Haas: Postgres 19 is late, and it's AI's fault
body:
PostgreSQL developer Robert Haas  writes
about the struggles  the project has encountered in putting together its
next release.
 
 
	In the end, I don't think that the delay in shipping PostgreSQL 19
	is particularly concerning. It is not a long delay in the grand
	scheme of things, and it emerges directly from the project's
	concern for quality.
 
	The long-term picture is less clear and in some ways more
	troubling: given that we have forty years of bugs that humans were
	unable to find but LLMs are quite capable of discovering, how are
	we ever going to catch up, and how will PostgreSQL continue to
	innovate? Right now, I'm not sure. What I do know is that I, and
	many others, are working really hard to figure it out.
 
 
LWN  looked at the PostgreSQL 19 release 
and its challenges in September.
